META.titleDoc: ESSENTIAL MATHEMATICS GRADE 10: AREA OF POLYGONS
META.subtitleDoc: OpenAI-only evaluation • Sub-Strand 2.4 • 11 lessons • teacher review copy

UNIT.sep: Measure,partition,derive,calculate and check geometric conditions and units.
UNIT.focus: Included-acute-angle and Heron triangles,parallelogram/rhombus,regularpentagon/hexagon,actual safe measurements and bounded applications.
UNIT.phenomenon: A fictional planner applies regular-pentagon formulas to every five-sided outline and treats any adjacent side as a height.
UNIT.supportingPhenomena: Actual paper triangles,valid/degenerate sides,angle-dependent parallelograms,diagonal partitions,regular central triangles and a tile-fit limit.
UNIT.drivingQuestion: Which dimensions and shape conditions justify a polygon area? KICD: How are areas of polygons useful?
UNIT.storylineThread: Includedangle → measure → Heron → validity/measure → parallelogram → rhombus → pentagon → hexagon → application → audit → independent evidence.
UNIT.content: Area of triangle; Area of rhombus and parallelogram.; Area of a pentagon and hexagon,
UNIT.coreCompetencies:
Creativity and Imagination: the learner acquires networking skills by undertaking group activities and exchanging new ideas while discussing discuss the applications of area of polygons.
Learning to learn: the learner learns independently when measuring the sides of a tringle and works out the area using the Heron’s Formula.
UNIT.values:
Unity: the learner shares available resources amicably while using selected objects with the shape of a regular pentagons and hexagon when working out the area.
Responsibility: the learner offers leadership to others while discussing with peers the applications of area of polygons
UNIT.pcis: Social Awareness Skills: the learner develops effective communication skills when discussing with peers the applications of area of polygons.
UNIT.subject: Essential Mathematics
UNIT.learningOutcomes:
compute area of a triangle given two sides and an included acute angle,
determine the area of a triangle given three sides using Heron’s Formula,
determine the area of a rhombus and parallelogram in different situations,
determine the area of regular pentagon and hexagon from real life situations,
appreciate the application of areas of polygons in real-life situations.

FINAL_EXPLANATION.instructions: Lesson11,40minutes:4procedure,12sections1–2,16sections3–4,4silentcheck,4collection. Work independently with PA11only,calculator in degree mode and blank paper. No teaching cards,peer work,hints or media. Show labelled geometry,formula substitution and squared units;round final nonexact areas to2decimalplaces.

sections.title: 1. Included-angle triangle area
sections.prompt: Draw FinalA,label its included acute angle and compute area using a derived perpendicular height or(1/2)ab sinC. Explain why the angle must be between the given sides and why the result uses square units.

sections.title: 2. Heron and a valid triangle
sections.prompt: For FinalB,check triangle feasibility,compute semiperimeter and use Heron’s formula to determine area. Explain why full perimeter cannot replace s and how a degenerate side set differs.

sections.title: 3. Parallelogram and rhombus
sections.prompt: Draw and compute both separate FinalCareas. Explain the perpendicular-height or diagonal-partition geometry and why the two data sets must not be combined into one shape.

sections.title: 4. Regular polygons and a useful area claim
sections.prompt: For FinalD,derive needed central/half angles or apothem and compute both areas. Explain why regularity is essential. Give a useful real-life area application and one limit such as measurement,fit or waste. Name one actual individual observation needed to certify your measurement skill.

SUMMARY_TABLE.drivingQuestion: Which dimensions and shape conditions justify a polygon area? KICD: How are areas of polygons useful?

lessons.title: Why must the two sides enclose the angle?
lessons.observed: Compute triangle area from two sides and their included acute angle.
lessons.learned: Perpendicular height equals the appropriate side times sine of the included angle.
lessons.explained: Draw,label,derive and calculate with squared units.

lessons.title: Can actual measurements check the sine-area method?
lessons.observed: Measure a real paper triangle and compare two area estimates.
lessons.learned: Actual dimensions carry instrument/rounding uncertainty and must not be replaced by ideal values.
lessons.explained: Construct/measure two sides,included angle and perpendicular height.

lessons.title: How does Heron use three sides?
lessons.observed: Determine triangle area with semiperimeter and Heron’s formula.
lessons.learned: A valid side set and a half-perimeter input are essential.
lessons.explained: Substitute,compute a radicand and check area units.

lessons.title: Can every three lengths form a triangle?
lessons.observed: Test side feasibility and use actual measured three-side data honestly.
lessons.learned: Strict triangle inequality and measurement uncertainty constrain a physical Heron result.
lessons.explained: Check validity,measure three sides and compare area estimates.

lessons.title: Which height belongs to a parallelogram base?
lessons.observed: Determine parallelogram area from adjacent sides and included angle.
lessons.learned: Area uses perpendicular height,not the sloping adjacent side.
lessons.explained: Compare two angle cases with the same side lengths/perimeter.

lessons.title: When do two rhombus area methods agree?
lessons.observed: Determine rhombus areas using side-angle and perpendicular diagonals.
lessons.learned: Rhombus diagonal partition and perpendicular height yield valid areas under their stated givens.
lessons.explained: Calculate and avoid combining incompatible separate designs.

lessons.title: How does regularity determine a pentagon area?
lessons.observed: Determine regular-pentagon area from side length via central triangles/apothem.
lessons.learned: Regularity fixes central/half angles and congruent triangle geometry.

lessons.title: Why does a regular hexagon split into equilateral triangles?
lessons.observed: Determine regular-hexagon area by two compatible partitions.
lessons.learned: A60degree central angle gives equal radius/side and a known apothem.
lessons.explained: Calculate central-triangle and apothem areas and compare.

lessons.title: What can a measured design area actually predict?
lessons.observed: Measure a safe regular template and connect area estimates to a bounded design use.
lessons.learned: Measured regularity,units and boundary fit constrain material/tiling claims.
lessons.explained: Record actual dimensions,calculate and explain a practical limit.

lessons.explained: Audit using a counterexample/formula and bounded application.
